inputs.original_text: Water deserves protection, but Alberta’s elected government—not a petition campaign—has the responsibility to make balanced decisions. Corb Lund’s Water Not Coal is demanding a legislative ban on all coal exploration, a sweeping move that risks putting ideology ahead of responsible development and the people who depend on it. Protecting the land and maintaining a strong resource economy are not mutually exclusive; elected leaders should reject slogans and govern in the public interest.
inputs.modified_text: The real issue is whether Alberta’s government will put water and affected communities ahead of coal-industry interests. Calling a demand for a ban on coal exploration “ideology” dismisses legitimate concerns about protecting shared resources; “balanced development” can become a cover for letting powerful extractive interests set the terms. Elected leaders have a responsibility to protect people and the land, not just defend a resource economy at any cost.
